newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency wants to limit release of credit data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency wants to limit release of credit data.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission recommended Monday that Congress tighten consumer confidentiality laws to help stop credit fraud and identity fraud.
It said current law did not bar credit bureaus from releasing identifying consumer information, yet such data might facilitate identity fraud, credit fraud or other illegal activities.
The agency said its proposal was a response to many consumer complaints and to inquiries by members of Congress, particularly Senator Richard Bryan, a Nevada Democrat.
It said the complaints concerned commercial services that provide identifying information about individuals for a fee.

The agency said that according to recent press reports, at least one tracking company currently furnished an individual's name, maiden name, aliases, prior addresses, telephone number, and birth month and year.
It said the tracking service had also furnished Social Security numbers.
The agency said in a letter to Bryan that fraud concerns outweighed the limited legitimate uses of this information for locating individuals.

It recommended that the Fair Credit Reporting Act be amended to provide confidentiality for a person's maiden name, Social Security number, prior addresses and date of birth, so this information would be released only to those with a legal release for obtaining it.
